summary: Implemented the print_json feature without running tests or repository code. Changes: rich/highlighter.py adds JSONHighlighter (base "json.", one combined pattern for brace, true/false/null, number, str). rich/json.py adds the JSON renderable (parse, re-serialize with indent, highlight or NullHighlighter, no_wrap=True, overflow=None, __rich__ returns text) plus a __main__ CLI block (file read failure prints "Unable to read" to stderr and exits -1; prints with soft_wrap=True). rich/console.py adds Console.print_json after print, importing JSON lazily. rich/__init__.py adds package-level print_json after print, delegating to get_console(); __all__ unchanged. rich/default_styles.py adds the six json.* keys. Docs: "Printing JSON" section in docs/source/console.rst, new docs/source/reference/json.rst, toctree entry in docs/source/reference.rst. CHANGELOG.md gets one Unreleased Added entry. Tests appended (existing tests untouched): test_print_json in tests/test_console.py and test_rich_print_json in tests/test_rich_print.py. Open points: the expected ANSI codes in test_print_json were derived by reading Style._make_ansi_codes, not by running, so verify them if it fails. Overflow is set to None per the spec's wording. The CLI must be run as python -m rich.json, because running the file directly would shadow the stdlib json module. Nothing was committed.
